The Trickle-Dry Effect
TL;DR: “Trickle-down” is debated; “trickle-dry” is observed everywhere but never named. When an anchor employer fails or leaves – a factory, shipyard, or mine – damage is immediate, asymmetric, and often irreversible. Restaurants close, property values crash, schools shrink, and original residents leave. If the company later recovers, recovery goes to newcomers, not those who held on. Cases from Gunsan (GM closure), Geoje (record profits with disconnected foreign labor), and Gangwon coal towns show the same cruel pattern.
Read more →

The Legibility Paradox
TL;DR: Between 1980 and 2026, the Korean won lost 40x domestic purchasing power, the dollar lost 4x, yet the exchange rate moved only 1.8x – because all major currencies fell together. This is the Rubber Ruler Problem: when every measuring stick shrinks, you cannot see the change. Korea’s dramatic transformation (GDP per capita from 1,700to1,700to35,000) made its currency legible while stable currencies hid their debasement. The Legibility Paradox: the currency cited as proof of monetary instability is the only one honest enough to bend visibly. Gangnam’s rise tracked real growth, not speculation.

The Bubble That Never Burst
TL;DR: For thirty years, analysts have called Gangnam a bubble – yet prices have risen 83.5 times while rice rose only 3.2 times. A bubble requires a crash, but Gangnam’s corrections (1991, 2008) were followed by new, higher floors. The three spikes (1988, 2002, 2018) each produced a staircase, not a return to origin. Korea’s five-century history of capital concentration (Dasan’s “live within 10 ri of Hanyang”) shows this is structural, not speculative. The true bubble was never Gangnam – it was the broken measuring stick used to judge it.

The Chip War Nobody Saw Coming – How Samsung Lost to SK Hynix
TL;DR: A viral anonymous Korean post argues Samsung lost its HBM lead not due to technology but governance failure. SK Hynix survived creditor-led crisis in the early 2000s, building a collaborative, crisis-forged culture. Samsung dissolved its central oversight body (MiJeonSil) after a political scandal, replacing it with a weak finance-focused task force. When engineers delivered world-first HBM4, management rewarded them with walnut cakes while executives got stock grants. That triggered mass unionization, a strike, and an ongoing battle over performance-based compensation. SK Hynix’s 2025 operating profit (₩47.2T) exceeded Samsung Electronics’ total (₩43.5T).

[News] Samsung Averts Largest Strike in Chip History With Last-Minute Bonus Deal (NEW)
TL;DR: Samsung and its 70,000-member union reached a tentative agreement 90 minutes before a planned 18-day walkout. The deal centers on a new “Special Management Performance Bonus” system: 10.5% of DS division operating profit for 10 years (2026–2035), paid entirely in company stock with phased vesting. SK Hynix’s February 2026 PS payout of 2,964% (~₩148M per employee) had set an impossible benchmark. Global DRAM supply at risk was 3-4%. Ratification vote: May 22-27, 2026.

South Korea’s Inheritance Tax – A Complete Guide
TL;DR: South Korea has one of the world’s highest inheritance taxes – 50% top rate, 60% for largest shareholders, second only to Japan in the OECD. The system uses an “estate tax” model (taxing the whole estate before distribution), unlike most OECD countries. Samsung’s Lee Kun-hee family paid ₩12.7 trillion ($9.3B) – the largest single inheritance tax bill ever. The Nexon family paid ₩6 trillion, transferring 29.3% of NXC shares to the government when no cash was available. A 2028 reform to shift from estate tax to acquisition tax has stalled.
Read more →

What the Numbers Don’t Tell You – Biyereyul (비례율)
TL;DR: Biyereyul is the ratio that determines how much money reconstruction association members must pay. The formula is simple, but all three variables are outside members’ control. In 6 cases with both initial and final figures, biyereyul dropped by an average of 16 percentage points – always downward, never up. One case saw members expecting a refund receive a demand for hundreds of millions of won just two months before move-in. The gap between initial estimate and final reality is where financial pain lives.

From Association to Relocation – Real Reconstruction Timelines (60 Projects)
TL;DR: Complete dataset of 60 reconstruction projects in Gyeonggi Province and Incheon that reached relocation. Shortest: Namyangju Hwado Prugio (2 years 9 months). Longest: Forena Incheon Guwol (9 years 1 month). Average: 5 years 11 months from association establishment to residents vacating the site. An additional table shows Seoul projects running 15-30 years, many still in progress. The projects that took the longest are not struggling neighborhoods – they are among the most sought-after addresses in South Korea.

The Rubber Ruler Problem
TL;DR: A student and professor dialogue: Gangnam’s 100x won increase becomes ~15x in real dollar terms after adjusting for inflation (won 40x, dollar 4x, exchange rate only 1.8x because all currencies fell together). Korea’s GDP per capita rose 20x over the same period – an apartment in the center of a country that grew 20x appreciated 15x in real terms. The “bubble” disappears when you realize the measuring stick was shrinking the whole time. The debate was never about Gangnam – it was about broken instruments.

How a Korean gaming giant’s CEO consulted ChatGPT instead of his lawyers (When the AI Took the Stand)
TL;DR: Krafton CEO Changhan Kim acquired Subnautica studio Unknown Worlds for 500Mwitha500Mwitha250M earnout clause. When the sequel looked like a hit, Kim’s legal team told him firing founders would not cancel the earnout. Kim consulted ChatGPT instead. The AI generated a “Response Strategy to a ‘No-Deal’ Scenario” – recommending preemptive PR, locking down Steam access, and legal preparation. The Delaware Court of Chancery quoted the ChatGPT conversations as block citations, found Kim acted in bad faith, reinstated the fired CEO, and extended the earnout window 258 days. AI chat logs are not privileged.

The Most Profitable Legal Business on Earth Is Making Sand Think
TL;DR: In Q1 2026, four AI infrastructure companies posted absurd margins: SK Hynix 72%, Samsung DS 65.7%, TSMC 58.1%, NVIDIA 75%. SK Hynix – a semiconductor manufacturer – posted higher margins than luxury goods houses. The driver is HBM (High Bandwidth Memory): structural supply constraints, multi-year fab lead times, and hyperscaler capex of ~$725B in 2026. A Korean forum user joked: “You couldn’t get 60% margins selling Han River water.” The joke was not hyperbole – it was structural analysis.

Profits Like NVIDIA, Valued Like a Steel Mill – The Korea Discount
TL;DR: Samsung (7x P/E) and SK Hynix (5x P/E) trade at a fraction of NVIDIA (21.8x) and TSMC (21.4x) despite higher margins. The “Korea Discount” has five official explanations, but a forum commenter cut to the core: “It’s the difference in how much you trust the country” (국가 믿음에 대한 차이지). On May 6, 2026, KOSPI broke 7,000, Samsung hit $1T market cap. Goldman’s KOSPI target is 8,000; JPMorgan’s bull case is 8,500. The question: is the Korea Discount closing?

The Citizen Who Beat a Law Firm with ChatGPT
TL;DR: Park Jang-ho was sued for ₩5.1 million in unpaid legal fees after his own lawyer withdrew and filed a criminal complaint for intimidation. He could not find new counsel (lawyers avoid opposing colleagues). Using general-purpose AI, he translated legal jargon, navigated Korea’s electronic litigation system, identified a missing signature and incorrect date in opposing counsel’s documents, and won both cases. Contrast with the Krafton CEO (who used AI after lawyers told him no, and lost). The distinction: Park used AI to reveal truth (document errors); Krafton used AI to evade obligation.

The Strike That Shouldn’t Be Happening – Inside Samsung’s Historic Labor Crisis
TL;DR: Samsung Q1 2026: ₩133.9 trillion revenue, ₩57.2 trillion operating profit – up 756% YoY – yet workers are striking. The National Samsung Labor Union (71,750 members, ~78% of workforce) demanded a fixed 15% of DS divisional profit as bonuses, and removal of the 50% salary cap. The deeper fracture: DS (semiconductor) workers earn near-max bonuses (47-50%), while DX (appliances) workers earn 12-15%. DS membership surged 3.5%; DX dropped 12.8%. Engineers are leaving for SK Hynix. Lee Jae-yong apologized in a parking lot after cutting a Japan trip short.

Why “We Can’t Do This Without You” Is a Warning
TL;DR: The professional trap is being known for a job function (“the investment analyst”) rather than a way of working (“translates complexity into decisions”). Organizations protect indispensable people – they do not develop them. The golden cage is comfortable, respected, locked from within. Identity foreclosure happens when expertise becomes identity. The solution is to brand yourself around how you work, not what you work on – building capital that travels.

https://seoulinside.substack.com/p/why-we-cant-do-this-without-you-is
The Capital You Can Actually Take With You
TL;DR: Career capital must be transferable, not just rare. Institutional knowledge that spends only inside one organization evaporates when the ground shifts. The T-shaped professional (deep expertise + coherent breadth) has the scarcity advantage in rooms full of specialists. Relational crafting – intentional cross-functional relationships – builds a map most peers lack. The question is not whether you will leave, but what you will have built by the time you do.
Read more → 
https://seoulinside.substack.com/p/the-capital-you-can-actually-take
What You Refuse to Give Up (Your Career Anchor)
TL;DR: Edgar Schein’s eight career anchors (Technical, Managerial, Autonomy, Security, Entrepreneurial, Service, Pure Challenge, Lifestyle) define what you would refuse to give up even for a promotion. Most professionals cannot answer honestly because the daily momentum of work actively blocks self-knowledge. Three kinds of stuckness: vertical (promoted out of your craft), value-based (the organization changes), relational (the golden cage). The gap between anchor and role is not always a reason to leave – it is always a reason to negotiate.
Read more → 
https://seoulinside.substack.com/p/what-you-refuse-to-give-up
How Wide Is Wide Enough?
TL;DR: Breadth without an organizing principle is just noise. Coherent breadth – a through-line across domains – predicts long-term advancement, not diversity of experiences. Real breadth requires enough engagement to see problems as practitioners in another domain see them, not just vocabulary. Relational crafting (one genuine cross-functional conversation per month, sustained) builds a map over time. Wide enough means: you can walk into a room of people who do not share your specialty and still be useful.
Read more → 
https://seoulinside.substack.com/p/how-wide-is-wide-enough
You Are Also a Draft (Job Crafting as Identity Architecture)
TL;DR: A hospital janitor named Luke timed his cleaning of comatose patients’ rooms to coincide with visiting hours – job crafting without a title change. Wrzesniewski’s three dimensions: task crafting (changing what you do), relational crafting (changing who you interact with), cognitive crafting (changing how you perceive your work). Small changes, sustained over time, produce large shifts in work identity. Most careers are not made in moments of rupture but in the accumulation of ordinary days. The cage is real. So is the key – it was always in your hands.
Read more → 
https://seoulinside.substack.com/p/you-are-also-a-draft
ILLIT’s Techno Turn Just Resurrected a 27-Year-Old Korean Hit
TL;DR: ILLIT’s 2026 hard techno “It’s Me” (No. 4 on Melon) led Koreans to rediscover Lee Jung-hyun’s 1999 “Wa” – too strange for its era but now visionary. Mashups went viral; Lee appeared in ILLIT’s challenge video in full 1999 costume, collapsing 27 years. Korean internet now calls her “Tapgol Lady Gaga” – an affectionate apology for not understanding her earlier. The stock of ILLIT’s agency trades below consensus due to a prior management dispute, not music quality.

Seoul Real Estate Has Always Been Unaffordable – Even 500 Years Ago
TL;DR: Primary sources from Joseon Korea confirm: even the Prime Minister (Yeongeuijeong) earned a salary paid in grain, insufficient to buy a house in Hanyang. Korea’s most revered scholar, Yi Hwang (Toegye), lived as a long-term renter – the word “imok” (賃屋, rented house) appears in his collected works. Dasan advised his sons to “live within 10 ri (4km) of the capital” because leaving meant permanent downward mobility. By 1754, yangban were seizing civilian homes by force, forcing King Yeongjo to crack down, then quietly compromise.
Read more → 
https://seoulinside.substack.com/p/seoul-real-estate-has-always-been
AI Thinks It Knows You – MIT Just Proved It Doesn’t
TL;DR: MIT researchers tested whether LLMs actually use all the information clients provide for investment advice. Across 1,000 synthetic client profiles, portfolio allocations were driven by a single variable: self-reported risk tolerance. Age, income, savings, horizon, liquidity, and debt had almost no measurable impact. The AI wrote personalized rationales – but the math underneath was not personalized at all. The researchers named this “Heuristic Collapse”: reducing multi-dimensional decisions to one salient feature.
Read more →
